title: skills/objectstack-data data-hooks.md: teach that an async write-event after-hook inside a unit of work runs after the commit and is dropped on rollback, while an async afterFind starts at dispatch
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5

Skills-docs follow-up owed by PR #34043 (card #33760, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`). This is the skills lane's file; the server lane does not edit `skills/**`.

**What the engine does after PR #34043.** For an `async: true` after-hook fired inside an engine-owned unit of work:
- On a write event (`afterInsert`, `afterUpdate`, `afterDelete`), the hook starts after the outermost commit, and is not run at all when the unit rolls back. A failed commit counts as a rollback.
- On `afterFind`, the hook starts at dispatch, outside the open units, as before. A rollback does not undo a read.
- Outside a unit, any async after-hook starts at once, as before.

**What the skill says now.** `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md:64`, in the Transaction row, says "in the background, after commit" for every async after-hook. That is inexact for `afterFind`. It also never teaches that a write-event async hook is dropped on rollback. An AI author will therefore still reach for an async hook to react to a refused or failed write, and that hook never fires.

**Ask:**
- Make the Transaction row event-precise: write events run after the commit and are dropped on rollback; `afterFind` runs at dispatch.
- Add one DON'T: to react to a failed write, use a blocking hook, not an async one.
- Exercise both in the skill's evals.
